clue.text: A sort of star at home, but unknown outside

indicators.note: the word for 'but' is placed outside the piece meaning 'at home', wrapping it

parts.note: bar, as a preposition, means except or but
in means at home
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone describes a type of star that is homely yet strangely unfamiliar to outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a preposition here, as in 'all bar one'; 'outside' wraps the 'but' word round the 'at home' word.
explanation.definitionFit: A binary star is a pair of stars orbiting each other, so it is one kind of star.

clue.text: Racing car bore singular, short name

parts.note: a drag is something tedious, a bore
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: short means the word for name loses its last letter

parts.note: a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: A dull, one-off racing car with a clipped name is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TERM to TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragster is a car built for drag racing over short straight tracks.

clue.text: Wave bands — four — which afford faster surfing

indicators.note: to wave is to move to and fro, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Bands of waves, four of them, giving surfers a quicker ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' rearranges BANDS and FOUR. The definition is a relative clause standing for 'things which afford faster surfing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Funboards are short, wide surfboards designed to give speed and manoeuvrability on waves.

clue.text: Learn something of verbal dexterity, say, in comeback

indicators.note: a comeback returns the way it came, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a piece of verbal cleverness
EG (for example) is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Someone learns a witty retort's wordplay in a quick reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in comeback' reverses both pieces together; 'say' is the usual signal for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gen up is British slang for learning about or studying a subject.

clue.text: No good blocking centre with barriers assembled

indicators.note: the abbreviation for no good sits inside the centre word, blocking it

parts.note: a core is a centre
gated means fitted with gates or barriers

explanation.surface: Something useless obstructs a barricaded central area where people gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' sets the no-good abbreviation inside the centre word; 'barriers' here means gates.
explanation.definitionFit: To congregate is to gather together, so congregated means assembled as a group.

clue.text: Place in SW France university's acquired a year in advance

indicators.note: in advance means the year piece comes before the university letter

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, a year
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A French town's university has obtained a year's funding ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquired' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pau is a town in the Pyrenees in south-western France.

clue.text: National network involves the tube — first class return

indicators.note: involves means the network word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
the tube is slang for television, TV

indicators.note: return means the first-class letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class

explanation.surface: A national railway network includes the Underground, with a first-class return ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses A1, and 'involves' wraps the network round the rest. 'the tube' looks like London's Underground but means television.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latvian is a national, a citizen of the Baltic state of Latvia.

clue.text: Admitting poet's not British

indicators.note: not means the British abbreviation is removed from the poet's name

parts.note: Robert Browning was a Victorian poet

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a poet's work isn't actually British.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing BR from BROWNING leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning up means admitting, so owning on its own can mean confessing.

clue.text: Dolly eyed by a drawer?

definitions.meaning: a dolly is an easy catch in cricket
a person posing who is studied by an artist sketching them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dolly' suggests a toy and 'drawer' furniture; both are false leads. In cricket a dolly is a very easy catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is both an easy cricket catch and an artist's model posing for a portrait.

clue.text: Robber somewhat taken aback, periodically concealed instrument

indicators.note: taken aback suggests going backwards, so the chosen letters are read in reverse
every other letter is kept while the rest are hidden, a regular pick

explanation.surface: A robber, a little startled, hid a musical instrument now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of 'Robber somewhat' gives OBROEHT; 'taken aback' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorbo is a large bass lute used in Baroque music, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Appeal to head of state finding some resistance

parts.note: O is a cry of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
HM, His or Her Majesty, is the British monarch

explanation.surface: A petition to the monarch meets some opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' is a link word. 'resistance' looks political but is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the unit of electrical resistance, so it measures some resistance.

clue.text: Bowler, ultimately, is harder on poor old county!

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Bowler
poor suggests something in bad shape, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bowler at the end of his career finds it harder in a poor old county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' shuffles the last three words, following the bowler's final letter. Radnorshire was a county in Wales, abolished in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Radnorshire was a Welsh county that no longer exists as an administrative area.

clue.text: More optimistic after heading off, one used to get weaving?

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the comparative is removed

parts.note: rosier means more hopeful or optimistic

explanation.surface: Someone feeling more upbeat sets off to start weaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get weaving' is an idiom for hurrying, but here it means literally weaving baskets.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow whose pliant shoots are woven into baskets and wickerwork.

clue.text: Level of cover, artificial as could be

indicators.note: artificial means made up rather than natural, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A level of cover as fake as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artificial' rearranges AS COULD BE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloud base is the height of the lowest cloud layer, the bottom level of cloud cover.

clue.text: Cardinal, one meeting Irish broadcaster visiting at the time

indicators.note: visiting means these pieces go inside the time word

parts.note: then means at that time
I is the Roman numeral one
RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: A Catholic cardinal meets an Irish broadcaster who is visiting at that time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' sets the numeral and broadcaster inside the time word. 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman but means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are counting numbers, and thirteen is one of them.

clue.text: Primate bestowing blessing on graduate

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a boon is a blessing

explanation.surface: A churchman gives a blessing to a new graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bestowing' is a link word. 'Primate' suggests an archbishop but means an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Baboons are large monkeys, members of the primate order of mammals.

clue.text: Glasses of basic lager initially drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests being thrown about, so these letters are mixed up
initially means just the first letter of lager is taken

explanation.surface: Glasses of plain lager have been drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges OF, BASIC and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifocals are spectacles with lenses divided for near and distant vision.

clue.text: Material is what Sue, Pat and Bob (unlike Ann) have brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.words: what Sue, Pat and Bob (unlike Ann) have
parts.note: these three names contain no letter N, while Ann does: they have no N in

explanation.surface: A fabric is what three friends, but not Ann, have raised.
explanation.walkthrough: The names have NO N IN them; 'brought up' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer fabric such as voile, used for curtains and dresses.

clue.text: Out loud, lament jumper that's shrunk

indicators.note: out loud means the word is as heard spoken

parts.note: to rue is to lament or regret

explanation.surface: Someone moans loudly about a sweater that shrank in the wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a British sweater, but it is a kangaroo, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Roo is a shortened form of kangaroo, an animal that jumps.

clue.text: Returned books to teacher for course

indicators.note: returned means the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
Sir is how pupils address a teacher

explanation.surface: Books have been handed back to the teacher for a course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: OT, TO and SIR are joined and reversed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a rice dish served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Giant score, and conversion, for club performers

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, of Gog and Magog

indicators.note: a conversion changes something into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge rugby score, plus a conversion, for the club's players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' rearranges SCORE AND into ODANCERS; 'score' and 'conversion' evoke rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-go dancers perform in nightclubs to entertain the crowd.

clue.text: Row about a lack of markers? Cook may need one

indicators.note: about means the row word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
no pen is a lack of something to mark with

explanation.surface: An argument over missing markers; a chef might need a kitchen tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NO PEN inside TIER. 'Row' suggests a quarrel but means a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook opening tinned food needs a device for cutting the lid off a can.

clue.text: Forcibly remove joint — not hard with hammer around

indicators.note: around means the hammer word wraps the other piece

parts.note: to hammer an opponent is to rout them

indicators.note: not means the hard letter is dropped from the joint word

parts.note: the hip is a joint
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone yanks out a joint, but not forcefully, with a hammer nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops hard from the joint, and 'around' wraps the hammer word round what is left; 'hammer' is a verb meaning beat soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip out is to tear something away violently, removing it by force.

clue.text: First thing in the morning banned from folding note

indicators.note: banned from means the morning abbreviation is excluded from the folding word

parts.note: origami is the art of paper folding
AM means in the morning
N is an abbreviation for note, as with footnotes

explanation.surface: First thing in the morning, folding a note is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banned from' removes the morning abbreviation from the folding art. 'First thing in the morning' looks like one phrase, but only 'First thing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the starting point or source, the first thing in a sequence.

clue.text: See in new light tenant with one in PR film

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the tenant word

parts.note: a renter is a tenant
I is the Roman numeral one
PR means public relations
ET is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A tenant appears with someone in a public-relations film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinterpret something is to understand or explain it differently, seeing it anew.

clue.text: Officials representing ancient Roman crowd?

parts.note: three's a crowd, so a Roman board of three officials could be called a crowd

explanation.walkthrough: The joke turns on the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the triumviri were boards of three magistrates or officials governing jointly.

clue.text: No surprise trees cut down at the end of the day by poet

indicators.note: cut down means the trees word loses its last letter

parts.note: a forest is a mass of trees

parts.words: at the end of the day by poet
parts.note: e'en is a poetic contraction of evening

explanation.surface: Unsurprisingly, the trees were felled at dusk by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims FOREST to FORES. 'cut down' suggests felling but means shortening the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foreseen was predicted beforehand, so its arrival is no surprise at all.

clue.text: Some, on reflection, feel CID arrest a bit of a nerve

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: On reflection, some feel that a police arrest takes a bit of nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in 'feel CID arrest' is ELCIDAR; 'on reflection' turns it around. CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a radicle is a small rootlike branch of a nerve, a tiny part of one.

clue.text: Got upset, did recruit, challenged

definitions.meaning: to carry on or fuss, become agitated

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions of one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Took on can mean became distressed, hired staff, or confronted a rival.

clue.text: Where an extra case may be added, on top of everything else

definitions.text: Where an extra case may be added
definitions.meaning: a suitcase can be put into a car's luggage compartment

explanation.walkthrough: A car's boot is its trunk, so a case may go 'to boot'.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot is an idiom meaning in addition, and literally a destination in a car's luggage space.

clue.text: State, audibly, one was equipped for gardening

indicators.note: audibly means the phrase is as heard spoken

parts.note: I'd a hoe, I had a garden tool

explanation.surface: A state, one hears, where someone was kitted out for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is "I'd a hoe".
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Turned up with a tiny bit of one's make-up

definitions.text: a tiny bit of one's make-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: and means with or plus

explanation.surface: Someone arrived with a little of their makeup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics but means genetic composition.
explanation.definitionFit: DNA is the genetic material that forms a person's biological make-up.
